feed.subtitle: EQUALS (Equitable Allocation of Low-carbon Electricity Sources in a Changing and Resource-limited World) is a 4-year research project funded by the French National Research Agency (ANR) under the Young Researcher (JCJC) programme (2025 call). The project is coordinated by Arthur Clerjon (CEA Liten, Grenoble). Official ANR page →

entry.title: We convened a breakout group at the Friburg 2026 Openmod workshop

link.title: We convened a breakout group at the Friburg 2026 Openmod workshop

entry.content:
We have been organizing an interactive workshop at the 2026 Openmod workshop in Freiburg, together with Pimprenlle PARMENTIER and Justine DUVAL.

The description of our intervention was the following:

Bringing Planetary boundaries and Energy Justice within Quantitative Modeling for energy planning

Description:

This workshop invites participants to play with an energy system optimization model and collectively experiment with ways of embedding energy justice, planetary boundaries and social foundations into energy planning.

The session is organized as a collective game on a representative European case, run with CAIRN, an open-source energy model. Participants will collaboratively define justice-oriented constraints and scenarios (sufficiency levels, resource limits, equity targets), implement them live in the model, and discuss the resulting trade-offs between technological choices, resource use and equity outcomes across a set of indicators. The aim is twofold: (i) to explore methods for collaborative, co-constructed scenario building, and (ii) to gather feedback from the modeling community on how planetary boundaries and energy justice can be operationalized within an ESOM.

The session will unfold in two phases:

  • A gameplay phase, where participants negotiate and evaluate trade-offs between indicators.
  • A discussion phase reflecting on the modeling methods and on the integration of planetary limits and justice into energy planning. cd

The link can be found here.

About 40 persons attended this workshop.

entry.title: We convened a breakout group at the 2026 Future Earth conference

link.title: We convened a breakout group at the 2026 Future Earth conference

entry.content:
We have been organizing an interactive workshop at the 2026 Future Earth Conference in Lausanne, together with Arthur CLERJON, Emmanuelle SANTOIRE and Justine DUVAL.

The description of our intervention was the following:

Operationalizing Energy Justice: Social Sciences and Quantitative Modeling for energy planning

Description:

This session proposes an interdisciplinary exploration of energy justice through the combined lenses of social sciences and quantitative modeling. It brings together expertise from energy system modeling and planning, energy geography, decision-support modeling, and the analysis of underground resource use, availability, and associated industrial developments. The session addresses a central challenge of contemporary energy transitions: translating the normative concept of energy justice into operational tools that inform energy planning and resource allocation. Designed as an interactive and participatory workshop, the session will engage participants in real-time modeling exercises, allowing them to explore how different justice-oriented constraints affect energy system outcomes and material requirements. By directly interacting with simplified planning models and resource-use frameworks, we will collectively examine trade-offs between technological choices, resource constraints, and equity considerations. A core objective of the session is to gather feedback from the audience in order to foster a collective reflection on how energy justice can be defined, interpreted, and operationalized through the lens of energy planning and resource use, thereby contributing to more transparent, inclusive, and just decision-making processes.
